summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's behavior, tone, or output format consistently, or encode domain-specific skills that prompting and RAG cannot reliably produce; it is not a substitute for supplying fresh or proprietary facts, which RAG handles better and cheaper. Reach for prompt engineering first, add RAG when the model needs external or up-to-date knowledge, and fine-tune only when you have enough high-quality labeled examples and measurable evaluation showing prompting/RAG fall short. Notably, a 2026 Theory Ventures survey found the share of teams that had ever fine-tuned fell from 81% to 51%, underscoring that fine-tuning is now a targeted tool rather than a default.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent style, format, or tone at scale (e.g., structured JSON outputs or a brand voice) that prompting cannot reliably enforce.
Fine-tune for narrow domain adaptation or specialized tasks (legal, medical, code) where you have hundreds to thousands of high-quality labeled examples.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when the core problem is supplying current, proprietary, or frequently changing facts to the model.
Only fine-tune after establishing a predefined evaluation showing prompt engineering and RAG genuinely underperform your quality or latency targets.
